text:
nate: FYI ran an nsys + perfetto pass on the kv-prefetch workload that triggered the perf regression from yesterday. seeing repeated H2D stalls around the KV refill window, looks tied to peer-copy bursts + pageable fallback. trace attached (nsys .qdrep).

marina: can you paste the timeline snippet where it spikes? curious if it's cudaMemcpyAsync or the peer-to-peer path. also which kernel set was active (fused-fp16-v2 or scalar-fp16)?

nate: snippet below from nsys timeline (abridged):
```
Time(ms)   Activity                         Size    Bandwidth
15432.2    memcpy H2D (pageable)             256MB   9.8 GB/s
15432.7    peerCopy GPU2->GPU1 (nvlink)      128MB   42 GB/s
15433.1    kernel: kv_prefill_fused_fp16_v2       ---   active
15433.5    memcpy H2D (pageable)             512MB   7.4 GB/s  <-- long tail, blocks host
15434.0    kernel: decode_batch_continuous     ---   queued
```
Overall pattern: big peercopy bursts immediately followed by large H2D pageable transfers that show long enqueue-to-complete gaps.

perf-bot: regression alert: kv-prefetch throughput -11% vs baseline (2028-10-03). Hotspot: host->dev memcpy and kernel_wait.

toni: paging behavior makes sense if host buffers are not registered. pageable memcpys drop to PCIe throughput and trigger CPU involvement. do we have code path that falls back to pageable for certain batch sizes?

nate: yes — batching heuristic will use pooled host buffers for small seqs but for long sequences (>=2048) we allocate from Python (non-registered) in the prefetch worker. that path was changed in the optimization PR (kernel selection refactor) to reduce pin churn but may have missed pre-register for the >2k path.

marina: that fits. so kernel selection change indirectly changed memory path -> more pageable transfers when certain kernels chosen. can you repro with env var RW_DISABLE_KERNEL_V2=1 to force old kernel?

nate: did that quickly: with RW_DISABLE_KERNEL_V2=1 the H2D tail disappears and host->dev bandwidth jumps to ~14 GB/s stable, and overall latency p50 drops 8%.

jas: nice bisect. do we have a minimal repro or a small script? would like to run nvprof too to capture API timelines.

nate: I'll push a tiny repro in gist after lunch. quick mitigation: pin the hot host buffers explicitly in prefetch worker (cudaHostRegister) or revert the kernel selection branch until we adjust the pooling logic.

toni: also consider enabling peer-to-peer memcpy for the GPUs involved (if topology supports) to avoid host bounce. NVLink peercopy numbers look healthy, but we still see a host bounce after the peer bursts — indicates some code path copies via host when cache eviction happens.

marina: could be KV cache eviction policy causing eager refill from CPU memory. if refill scheduling batches de-duped prefixes poorly, we might create large simultaneous refills. can you dump the refill batching windows?

nate: added a short log snippet from the runtime (timestamps in ms):
```
[15432.100] refill: gpu1 ids=512 size=4MB
[15432.110] refill: gpu2 ids=512 size=4MB
[15432.115] refill: peercopy start gpu2->gpu1 128MB
[15432.120] refill: host_alloc (pageable) 512MB
[15432.360] refill: host->dev memcpy start (blocked)
```
Shows simultaneous refills from both GPUs leading to overlapping H2D windows.

perf-bot: suggestion: throttle refill concurrency to 1 per-host or add jitter to refill events to smooth PCIe usage.

marina: agree. long-term fix: ensure prefetch uses pinned buffers from the pool for all refill size classes and update pooling to preallocate for worst-case seq length. short-term: cap concurrent refills and enable cudaHostRegister where easy.

nate: creating a PR to re-add registration + limit concurrency to 2. will include nsys traces before/after. tagging @marina for review.

toni: when you push traces, include perfetto flame (host-side) so we can correlate worker thread blocking with enqueue delays. nvlink vs pcie distinction was clear in nsys but need host timeline to prove host-blocking.

nate: noted. thanks all. will follow up with PR and a small repro gist. :v:
